help.doctor:
Usage: rigorkit doctor

Reports the health of your installations without changing them:
the clone's version and local changes, custom scripts and packs that shadow
official ones, the global record's version with its edited or missing copies
and packs no longer shipped, and for every registered project its version,
whether it is outdated, installed from a development clone, has edited
copies, or no longer exists.

The only repair is the execute bit of official helper scripts in the clone;
custom scripts are only reported.

Options:
  --help                Show this help

Examples:
  rigorkit doctor

Writes:
  Nothing, except the execute bit of official helper scripts.

Exit status: 0 when nothing needs attention, 1 when something does
(outdated, edited, missing, shadowing, local changes, unreadable records,
packs recorded but no longer shipped),
2 for invalid arguments.
help.help:
Usage: rigorkit help [<command>]

Shows the list of commands, or the help of one command.

Options:
  --help, -h            Show this help

Examples:
  rigorkit help
  rigorkit help install

Writes:
  Nothing.
help.install:
Usage: rigorkit install --pack <packs> --agent <agents> [--project <dir> | --global] [options]
       ./install.sh <same options>

Installs packs (skills, agents and, with --global, rules) into each coding
agent's folders. Packs come from this clone and from ~/.rigorkit/custom/packs;
a custom pack replaces the official pack with the same name.

Options:
  --pack <packs>        Comma-separated packs, or 'all' (official and custom)
  --agent <agents>      Comma-separated: claude, codex, cursor, opencode
  --project <dir>       Install into a project folder (default: current folder)
  --global              Install into your home folder, including global rules
  --force               Overwrite skills and agents that already exist
  --dry-run             Print what would change; write nothing
  --uninstall-rules     Remove rigorkit rule blocks from the global rule files
  --version             Print the version of this clone
  --list                List packs and what each one installs
  --help, -h            Show this help

Examples:
  rigorkit install --pack core,sdd --agent claude --global
  rigorkit install --pack all --agent claude,codex --project ~/code/app --dry-run
  rigorkit install --uninstall-rules --agent claude

Writes:
  <scope>/.claude/skills, <scope>/.agents/skills   skills
  <scope>/.claude/agents, .cursor/agents, .codex/agents, .opencode/agents
                                                  agents (OpenCode global: ~/.config/opencode/agents)
  <scope>/.rigorkit-version                       installed version
  ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md
                                                  global rules, between rigorkit markers,
                                                  with a <file>.rigorkit.bak backup
  ~/.local/state/rigorkit/global                  with --global: what was installed, for rigorkit update
  <scope> is the project folder, or your home folder with --global.
help.rigorkit:
Usage: rigorkit <command> [args]

Commands:
  install [options]      Install packs into your coding agents (same as install.sh)
  update [--dry-run]     Move to the newest release and refresh your global scope
  scan [<folder>...]     Find installed projects and register them for updates
  doctor                 Report versions, edited copies and problems (read-only)
  script <name> [args]   Run a helper script, custom first, then official
  help [<command>]       Show this list, or the help of one command

Run 'rigorkit help <command>' or 'rigorkit <command> --help' for details.
Manual: man rigorkit. If 'rigorkit' runs an older copy, check which one comes
first in PATH with 'command -v rigorkit'.
help.scan:
Usage: rigorkit scan [--dry-run] [--save] [--tools <list>] [<folder>...]

Finds the projects where rigorkit is installed (folders holding
.rigorkit-version, up to 4 levels below each folder) and registers each new
one in ~/.local/state/rigorkit/projects, so rigorkit update can update them.
It first lists every new project with the tools suggested from its folders,
then asks once: y registers all of them with those tools, e asks project by
project (Enter accepts the suggestion, - skips it), n registers none. Copies that
match a 0.1.0 release keep their fingerprint; copies you edited are marked
so later updates ask before replacing them. Projects already registered are
left as they are.

Without folders it scans scan_paths from ~/.config/rigorkit/config
(comma-separated, ~ allowed) and never enters .git, node_modules or the
names in scan_exclude:
  scan_paths=~/workspace
  scan_exclude=archive,dist

Options:
  --dry-run             Show what would be registered; ask and write nothing
  --save                Add the given folders to scan_paths
  --tools <list>        Tools for every new project (claude,codex,cursor,opencode)
  --help                Show this help

Examples:
  rigorkit scan --save ~/workspace
  rigorkit scan
  rigorkit scan --dry-run --tools claude ~/code

Writes:
  New project records in ~/.local/state/rigorkit/projects and, with --save,
  the scan_paths line of ~/.config/rigorkit/config. Nothing inside projects.

Exit status: 2 for invalid options or no folder to scan, 3 when a folder
does not exist.
help.script:
Usage: rigorkit script <name> [args]

Runs the first helper script named <name> from, in order:
~/.rigorkit/custom/scripts, the custom packs' scripts folders, and the
official packs' scripts folders not replaced by a custom pack (packs in
name order). Every argument after <name> is passed to the script unchanged,
and rigorkit exits with the script's status.

Options:
  --help                Show this help (only as the first argument)

Examples:
  rigorkit script test-summary npm test
  rigorkit script json-peek package.json 2

Writes:
  Nothing; the script itself may write.

Exit status: 2 for a missing or invalid name, 127 when no script has that
name, 126 when the script found first is not executable.
help.update:
Usage: rigorkit update [--dry-run]

Moves ~/.rigorkit to the newest release (vX.Y.Z tag of its remote), shows the
changelog of every version in between, then refreshes your global scope and
the projects registered by rigorkit install --project or rigorkit scan. It
refuses when the clone has local changes (move them to ~/.rigorkit/custom),
when the newest tag does not descend from your clone, or when the tag's
VERSION does not match its name. Only one update runs at a time.

Options:
  --dry-run             Fetch the newest release and show the changelog and
                        every question with its diff; ask nothing, write
                        nothing outside ~/.rigorkit/.git
  --help, -h            Show this help

Questions (each one writes only on a yes; anything else is a no):
  Rewrite the rigorkit startup block in <file>?       one per startup file
  Update <n> unedited global copies?                  one for all of them
  Rewrite the rigorkit block in <file>?               one per rules file, with the diff
  <path> was edited. Overwrite or keep? [o/k]         one per edited copy, with the diff: overwrite or keep;
                                                      keep is remembered until it changes again
  Install new pack <pack> globally ...?               one per pack new in the changelog
  Remove <n> old rigorkit scripts from ...?           ~/.local/share/rigorkit/scripts
  Remove the record of <path>?                        a registered project folder that no longer exists
  Update project <path> (<old> -> <new>)?             one per outdated project; its unedited copies are
                                                      replaced, edited ones asked overwrite or keep
  <path> was installed from the development clone ... one per project installed from another clone
  Rename specs/backlog.md to specs/roadmap.md in <path>?
  Without a terminal every question is answered no and the skipped items are listed.

Writes:
  ~/.rigorkit (except custom/), its git data and ~/.local/state/rigorkit/
  ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile            startup block, with a <file>.rigorkit.bak backup
  registered projects                             skill and agent copies, .rigorkit-version and the
                                                  backlog.md rename; never committed or staged
  ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md
                                                  global rules, between rigorkit markers,
                                                  with a <file>.rigorkit.bak backup
  ~/.claude, ~/.agents, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, ~/.config/opencode
                                                  global skills and agents
  ~/.local/share/rigorkit/scripts                 old scripts it removes

Update check (at shell start and when rigorkit runs, at most once per period),
set in ~/.config/rigorkit/config as key = value lines:
  update_mode = prompt     ask at shell start whether to update (default)
  update_mode = reminder   print one line at shell start and in rigorkit runs
  update_mode = disabled   no check and no notice
  update_days = 1          days between checks, a whole number of at least 1

Examples:
  rigorkit update --dry-run
  rigorkit update
